archetype: USD spot as the cleanest benchmark

conflict_synopsis.core_view: The CA-US yield gap is historically extreme versus only a moderate USDCAD percentile, so own the view in USD spot versus CAD.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Fed tightening bias stays intact while BoC does not match and the Saudi workaround caps CAD's oil-tail hedge.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: CA-US 2Y compresses via a BoC hike or Fed easing, or a renewed oil-supply tail restores CAD terms-of-trade dominance.

remit: express macro views through USD spot whenever a defensible USD pair exists
stance_summary: Own the US-Canada policy and front-end gap in USDCAD spot; crosses and AUD/NZD USD pairs add second-order risk or fight carry.

catalysts: Further US inflation or labor prints that keep the Fed tightening bias intact
BoC communication that energy pass-through does not force a matching hike
Evidence the Saudi workaround continues to cap the extreme oil-supply tail
Global term-premium pressure from BoJ tightening and BoE QT
trade.horizon: Tactical 2-8 weeks; keep the USD-over-CAD stance while the CA-US 2Y gap remains historically wide versus USDCAD’s more moderate percentile.
trade.invalidation: The causal mechanism fails if the CA-US 2Y gap compresses because the BoC hikes on energy pass-through or US front-end yields fall as the Fed’s tightening bias breaks, or if CAD terms of trade re-dominate via a renewed oil-supply tail.
trade.mispricing: Markets have started to mark USD higher versus CAD but still treat CAD as energy-supported. That is inconsistent with a CA-US 2Y gap at the 4th percentile of the 1y distribution while USDCAD itself is only around the 74th 1y percentile.
principal_risks: CAD terms-of-trade support from crude near $110
BoC energy pass-through risk could force a Canadian hike
Canada Q2 GDP +0.8% q/q is a growth offset
Positioning and executable broker prices are absent
trade.thesis: The economically relevant discrepancy is the CA-US yield gap versus USDCAD, not a commodity-cross or an AUD housing story. After the Fed's delivered 25bp hike, US 2Y sits at 4.67% against CA 2Y at 3.27%. The CA-US 2Y spread is -140bp at the 3.8th 1y percentile. USDCAD is only 74th percentile 1y with a +1.74% 1m gain that has not closed a still-negative 3m return. Energy still supports CAD ToT, but the Saudi workaround reduced the extreme oil-supply tail. Crosses do not own this: AUDCAD is already 99.8th percentile 1y, NZDUSD has already fallen 3.90% over 1m, and short AUDUSD fights a still-positive AU-US 2Y of +26bp.
why_now: The September 16 Fed hike is now realized, not just a >90% priced event.
The CA-US 2Y spread widened 15bp over five days and 17bp over one month.
The last24 desk thesis dated 2026-09-18 states BoJ tightening and a hawkish BoE hold broadened global tightening after the Fed.
Saudi ship-to-ship crude via Oman reduced the extreme oil-supply tail that had been CAD’s best fundamental offset.
